title: Can an angle describe how steep a slab is?
description: A toy has slanting slabs with balls that roll down them. The edge of a slab is one arm, a line straight across from its top is the other arm, and a larger angle is checked against a faster ball.
teaching_notes: One idea: the slope of a slab is an angle between its edge and a line straight across from its top. Watch for students who look for both arms drawn on the toy.

source: Figure it Out: Where are the angles?, Q4
video_script.why: The child finds the two arms of an angle in a real toy, one visible and one not drawn, and links a larger angle with a steeper slope.
video_script.substitution: The slanting slabs of the book's toy.
video_script.anchor: the toy of the book with slanting slabs attached to its sides and balls that roll down them
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, a larger angle means a greater slope

final_answer.value: Yes; a larger angle means a greater slope; the edges of the slabs are visible arms, and the top horizontal ray is not visible
final_answer.spoken: a larger angle means a greater slope

maths_rules: the edge of a slab is one arm of the angle, and it is visible
the other arm is the top horizontal ray, which is not drawn on the toy
a larger angle means a greater slope, and balls roll faster on a greater slope
video_script.design: The toy stays on the board. The edge of a slab lights up as the visible arm, then a dotted line straight across from its top is drawn as the arm that is not visible, and the word horizontal is held back until the answer line.
open_questions: The toy is a drawn figure that is not in the extracted text. The book's solution says both that the vertical arm is not visible and that the top horizontal ray is not visible; the video follows the worklist, the top horizontal ray.
